items.title: Straight From the (AI) Source: Is AEO/GEO different than SEO?
items.summary: Insights from Google, Microsoft, and AI platforms show AEO/GEO builds directly on SEO foundations, emphasizing useful, original, crawlable content without spammy tactics. No major differences; strong SEO ensures visibility in AI Overviews and Copilot via retrieval-augmented generation. Focus remains on user-first practices rather than AI-specific hacks.

items.title: Media Do Agrees to Buy Seven Seas Entertainment
items.summary: Japan's Media Do International has agreed to acquire Seven Seas Entertainment, one of the largest independently owned manga publishers in North America. The deal, announced recently, aims to strengthen Media Do's position in the English-language manga market amid growing demand. This acquisition reflects ongoing consolidation in the publishing industry.

items.title: Rights Report: Week of February 23, 2026
items.summary: Publishers Weekly details several new book acquisition deals from the week, including children's titles with North American rights sold to major houses like Macmillan. Agents brokered deals for publication in 2027 and later. The report showcases active deal-making in children's and young adult publishing.

items.title: JW Radford Signs Three-Book Publishing Deal with Poppy Grace Publishing
items.summary: Author JW Radford has inked a three-book deal with Poppy Grace Publishing, marking a key milestone in their career. The first book under the agreement is slated for release by the end of the year. This contract highlights opportunities for emerging authors in niche publishing.

items.title: Romantasy & The Downfall Of BookTok
items.summary: A Her Campus article argues that the romantasy boom, fueled by BookTok, is leading to the platform's decline due to oversaturation and quality concerns. It critiques popular titles like Fourth Wing amid community debates. The piece reflects tensions between viral trends and literary standards on BookTok.

items.title: New Self-Publishing Podcast Examines Controversy Surrounding AI-Generated Romance Novels
items.summary: Alliance of Independent Authors (ALLi) releases a podcast where Dan Holloway analyzes a New York Times report on AI-generated romance novels dominating self-publishing platforms. The discussion covers the explosion of low-effort AI books and their threat to human authors. It sparks wider debate on AI's role in writing and publishing.

items.title: Publisher Terminates $45 Million Contract with Donald Trump
items.summary: Simon & Schuster has terminated Donald Trump's $45 million book deal after years of missed deadlines and no manuscript delivery. Warren Buffett speaks out on the high-profile publishing fallout. The cancellation underscores risks in blockbuster political book contracts.

items.title: BookTok Erupts Over Viral 'Fast-Fashionified' Books Criticism
items.summary: A viral video claiming romantasy books on BookTok have been 'fast-fashionified' ignites fierce debate in the community. Critics argue it devalues literature, while defenders highlight accessibility. The controversy underscores evolving dynamics in BookTok trends.

items.title: ‘Scream 7’ Actor Anna Camp Apologizes for Sharing Post That Hit Back at Boycotts Over Melissa Barrera Firing
items.summary: Anna Camp reposted content celebrating Scream 7's box office success despite boycotts related to Melissa Barrera's firing for social media posts, but deleted it and apologized, stating it did not reflect her beliefs. The film opened to $64.1 million domestically, setting a franchise record amid protests at its premiere. Online reactions highlighted divisions over the boycott's failure.

items.title: Disney Pixar Removes 'Woke' Content After Recent Protests
items.summary: Pixar scaled back environmentalist messaging in its upcoming film Hoppers to focus on character-driven storytelling following criticism of agenda-driven content in prior releases like Lightyear. The changes aim to broaden appeal amid debates over political themes in Disney animation. Early reviews are positive with a 97% Rotten Tomatoes score ahead of its March 6 release.

items.title: ‘A Knight of Seven Kingdoms’ Actress Responds to Racial Backlash About Her Role
items.summary: Tanzyn Crawford, playing Tanselle in HBO's Game of Thrones prequel A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms, addressed social media backlash criticizing her casting amid praise for the show's 'non-woke' focus on white male leads. She emphasized pursuing her dreams and noted George R.R. Martin's approval of her fit for the character. The controversy highlights tensions over diversity in the fantasy series.

items.title: Scary Movie 6 Trailer Sparks Backlash Over Pronoun Joke
items.summary: The Scary Movie 6 trailer, released March 2, opens with a joke about pronouns that drew online criticism for mocking non-binary identities. Reactions split between those calling it dated and others praising the parody of modern sensitivities. The film is set for theaters on June 12.

items.title: A 'Game of Thrones' Movie Is in Development at Warner Bros.
items.summary: Warner Bros. is developing a Game of Thrones movie from House of Cards showrunner Beau Willimon and Andor writer. The project expands the franchise following the success of HBO prequels. Details on plot and cast remain under wraps.

items.title: 'Deadliest Catch' Deckhand Todd Meadows Dies During Filming
items.summary: Deckhand Todd Meadows passed away during production of Deadliest Catch, as reported by Deadline. The incident occurred amid filming, prompting tributes from the reality TV community. Discovery Channel has not detailed circumstances.

items.title: Amazon’s new AI experience helps sellers visualize and grow their business in real time—here's how it works
items.summary: Amazon has introduced a canvas experience in Seller Central, powered by agentic AI and Amazon Bedrock, that allows sellers to generate personalized, interactive visual workspaces integrating their business data, insights, and recommended actions in real time. This tool enables sellers to analyze performance trends, optimize marketing campaigns, make inventory decisions through scenario simulations, and plan product launches by exploring historical sales, customer insights, and competitive data. Available at no additional cost to U.S. and U.K. sellers, the canvas adapts to follow-up questions, providing tailored visualizations and projections to support data-driven decisions for business growth.

items.title: Meta Explores AI-Powered Shopping Research Tool
items.summary: Meta is testing an AI-powered shopping research tool within its AI chatbot, available to some American users of Meta’s AI web browser, which provides product suggestions including images, brand details, prices, and merchant links based on user queries. The recommendations are tailored to the user’s location when applicable, though the tool does not support direct checkout or payments. This development is relevant to businesses as it aligns with Meta’s goal of offering personalized shopping experiences and could enhance eCommerce by directing users to merchant sites, potentially increasing traffic for brands in Meta’s catalog.

items.title: Redefining hard work in the AI era
items.summary: Small businesses are using AI to reduce time on administrative tasks, with 91% reporting less time spent on such work and 73% integrating it across core operations like marketing, design, staffing, customer engagement, and security. Founders apply AI practically by offloading repetitive tasks, such as drafting emails, proposals, or meeting notes, to free up focus for higher-value activities. AI serves as a creative partner and research assistant, creating headspace for better decision-making and strategic thinking rather than just efficiency.
